newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says foreign private debt under control.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says foreign private debt under control.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said foreign private debts were at a controllable level despite their increases.
"...the increase of foreign private debts is still within controllable limits although they are on the rise," Djiwandono told a parliament hearing on Wednesday.
He said they were controllable from the point of view of the national economic capacity, of the balance of payments and also of the percentage of short-term loans to total foreign debts.
He said the current debt-service-ratio, indicator for the ability to meet principal and interest payments, was 14.6 percent for offshore government debts and 19.6 percent for foreign private debts.
"Declining exports and rising private offshore loans were responsible for the increase of the debt-service-ratio."
Djiwandono said, however, the government was trying to control offshore borrowing by narrowing domestic saving gaps and increasing the country's export ability.
The governor said Bank Indonesia had simplified reporting methods to get more firms to inform the bank of any new loans.
He said the bank had also issued Yankee bonds in July last year to help Indonesian companies get better spreads after a benchmark was established through the government bonds.
Djiwandono said short-term loans, less than one year, accounted for only 9.1 percent, or $9.1 billion, of the total outstanding foreign loans of $109.3 billion.
